why:
Most commands hold up. Both briefs name tracked files: bin/jsonl-lint.js, src/index.js, test/cli.test.js, test/lint.test.js, README.md and .github/workflows/test.yml. `readFileSync(0,'utf8')`, spawnSync with `input`, `npm ci` (a package-lock.json exists), `npm test --workspace packages/jsonl-lint`, `node --test packages/jsonl-lint/test/lint.test.js` and the printf/gh/git commands are all valid.

The failure is in the verifier brief. It sets B to the repo-relative path `packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js`, then has the verifier make a scratch dir for c1.jsonl, c2.jsonl and b.jsonl. It then runs `node B c1.jsonl b.jsonl c2.jsonl` and similar commands. Run from the repo root, the bare scratch file names don't resolve. Run from the scratch dir, B doesn't resolve. No single working directory makes those commands work as written. The verifier would have to use an absolute path for B or a scratch-dir prefix on each file.
